headline: US stocks closed lower as strong August jobs data boosted Fed hike odds and lifted short‑term yields ahead of next week’s CPI and PPI releases
raw_text:
- The S&P 500 (SPX) fell 0.4% to 7,718.60, the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJI) lost 0.5% to 53,414.25, the Nasdaq Composite (COMP) slipped 0.3% to 26,506.99, while the Russell 2000 (IWM) rose 0.2% to 2,975.65 and the S&P 500 (SPX) finished the week essentially flat.
- U.S. nonfarm payrolls increased by 162,000 in August versus roughly 56,000 expected, with the unemployment rate steady at 4.1%, leading traders to price in over a 50% chance of a September Federal Reserve rate hike.
- The 2‑year Treasury yield rose to 4.37% following the stronger‑than‑expected jobs report, reflecting higher near‑term rate expectations.
- Industrials led the S&P 500 (SPX) with a 0.41% gain, supported by strength in Eaton (ETN) and J.B. Hunt (JBHT).
- Consumer discretionary stocks underperformed, falling about 1.3%, as Lululemon Athletica (LULU) dropped 17.4% after Q2 revenue of $2.42 billion and a 9% same‑store sales decline missed estimates and the company cut full‑year revenue and EPS guidance.
- Tech and memory names outperformed, with SanDisk (SNDK) up 11.9%, Micron Technology (MU) gaining 6.1% on AI memory demand, and Nvidia (NVDA) up 0.8% amid rising AI equity investments.
- In extended trading, Bloom Energy (BE) jumps 6.2% after S&P Dow Jones Indices said it will be added to the S&P 500 (SPX) effective September 21 alongside Illumina (ILMN) and Everpure (P).
- Investors now look to next week’s CPI and PPI reports for further signals on Federal Reserve policy, with U.S. markets closed Monday for the Labor Day holiday.
